content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken meat grilled without added sauce is a lean source of protein. It is rich in B‑vitamins, minerals (iron, zinc, phosphorus) and contains very little fat when no oil is used during cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken is the most widely consumed poultry worldwide, featured in virtually every cuisine.
Grilling imparts a characteristic smoky flavor through Maillard reactions while leaving the natural taste intact without sauce.
Skinless grilled chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein and less than 3 g of fat per 100 g.
Chicken is a good source of collagen, which turns into gelatin during cooking and supports joint health.
Proper grilling preserves most vitamins compared with deep‑frying, which can cause greater nutrient loss.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth and repair, supports the immune system and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Absence of skin and sauce makes the dish suitable for low‑fat and calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B3 (niacin) and B6 play key roles in energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation, immunity and bone health.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: A complete amino‑acid profile helps maintain and build muscle, especially for active individuals.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Insufficient cooking may leave harmful bacteria such as Salmonella or Campylobacter alive.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: A small number of people can develop allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the meat was previously marinated, sodium levels can be high; plain grilling without added salt is preferable.

items.title: Formation of carcinogens
items.content: Excessive charring on the grill can produce heterocyclic amines; aim for a golden brown crust rather than black char.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless grilled chicken can be served as a main dish, sliced into salads, added to soups, wraps, or used as a sandwich filling. It pairs well with vegetables, lemon, herbs and light yogurt‑based sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw chicken refrigerated at ≤ 4 °C for no more than 2 days, and cooked meat in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at ‑18 °C; thaw in the refrigerator before use.
